title: Career roadmap · Professor
summary: Build an academic career in urban science by combining spatial analysis, mobility, urban systems, infrastructure, data science, sustainability and policy research with strong teaching and grant leadership.

facts.Timeline assumption: The roadmap assumes a 2026-start Ph.D. research pathway. The first phase develops a rigorous interdisciplinary research identity; the post-Ph.D. phase focuses on independent research, publications, teaching, grants, supervision and urban-policy impact.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build expertise in urban systems, GIS, spatial data, mobility, statistics, sustainability and smart-city technologies.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Establish an independent research niche such as urban mobility, spatial AI, climate-resilient cities, urban economics or smart infrastructure.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead a research laboratory or centre, supervise doctoral researchers and secure interdisciplinary urban-research funding.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Shape urban research agendas, advise governments and cities, lead centres and integrate AI, climate adaptation and emerging mobility systems into research and teaching.

blocks.text: Ph.D. routes

The senior academic target is to lead a durable urban research program rather than remain a specialist in one technology. Build collaborations across planning, engineering, computer science, economics, environmental science and public policy. The strongest research agenda should connect spatial and mobility data to measurable outcomes such as accessibility, safety, resilience, affordability, emissions and quality of life.
